user.title: Show PIP on an LG webOS TV
user.description:
Pick the TV (from the LG webOS TV integration). The HA PIP app must be installed on it; see the README.

The URL and access token are optional. When set, they are sent to the TV app so you don't have to type the token with the remote.

data.ha_url: Home Assistant URL as seen from the TV
data.token: Long-lived access token for the TV app

data_description.ha_url: Usually your internal URL, e.g. http://192.168.1.10:8123. Don't use homeassistant.local if the TV can't resolve it.
data_description.token: Create it under your profile → Security → Long-lived access tokens. A dedicated non-admin user is a good idea.
data_description.mode: MJPEG works best over live TV. HLS and WebRTC need a second video decoder, which depends on the TV.
data_description.size: PIP width as a percentage of the screen width.
data_description.timeout: Seconds until the PIP closes itself. 0 keeps it open until closed.
data_description.app_id: Only change this if you built the TV app with a different ID.

abort.no_tv: No LG webOS TV found. Set up the LG webOS TV integration first.
abort.already_configured: PIP is already set up for this TV.

user.title: PIP trigger
user.description: When one of the entities changes to the trigger state while the TV is on, show a camera or URL on the TV.

data_description.trigger_entities: e.g. a doorbell binary sensor or event entity.
data_description.trigger_state: Leave empty: binary sensors, switches and input booleans fire on "on", everything else (e.g. event entities) on any change.
data_description.url: Instead of a camera: an HLS (.m3u8), MJPEG or video URL, or an HA path like /media/local/clip.mp4.
data_description.title: Text shown in the PIP. Defaults to the camera name.
data_description.mode: Leave empty to use the TV's default.
data_description.position: Leave empty to use the TV's default.
data_description.size: Leave empty to use the TV's default.
data_description.timeout: Leave empty to use the TV's default.
